events.title: Start-of-year department meeting
events.description: The department meets the week before classes start. It is the best place to meet colleagues and hear the year's priorities.
events.tip: Bring questions about coordinated courses and your syllabus.

events.title: Syllabus due
events.description: Send your syllabus to the Head of Department (cc the department assistant). For coordinated courses, your course coordinator approves it first.
events.tip: Start from the department template and check the coordinator's shared materials.

events.title: Faculty Research Grant (FRG) call opens
events.description: Internal grants of up to AED 500,000 over two years. Read the call, then plan your proposal and budget with your Head of Department.
events.tip: Attend the Q&A session if one is announced.

events.title: Sabbatical applications
events.description: Applications move from Head of Department to Dean, Provost, a committee and the Chancellor. Plan early because each step has its own deadline.
events.tip: Talk to your Head of Department in the first weeks of term.

events.title: FRG proposal: deadline to the Dean
events.description: Principal investigators send the proposal to the Dean. The School then submits it to the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research.
events.tip: Allow time for IRB needs and a budget check before the deadline.

events.title: SBA Undergraduate Research Grant, round 1
events.description: Supports faculty who involve undergraduate students in research. A second round follows in the Spring.
events.tip: A good first grant to try with a student collaborator.

events.title: Midterm grades for at-risk students
events.description: Enter midterm grades in Banner for students who are struggling, so advisors can reach them early.
events.tip: Faculty Services > Midterm Grades in Banner.

events.title: Commencement faculty attendance
events.description: Faculty are asked to confirm whether they will attend commencement.
events.tip: Watch for the email from the Dean's office.

events.title: Advising for Spring
events.description: Meet your advisees and clear their advising holds. The Management major map shows the course sequence and prerequisites.
events.tip: Open the major map during the meeting and plan the next two semesters.

events.title: Promotion and rolling contract: how the timeline works
events.description: Second contract: assessed before the last academic year of the first three-year contract. Rolling contract: in-depth review in the sixth year of full-time employment (up to two years of credit may apply). Promotion: eligible after five years in rank, with at least one year under a full-time AUS contract. Early promotion needs a written supporting report. Annual assessments happen at the end of Spring. The Provost sets the exact deadlines at the start of each academic year.
events.tip: Ask your Head of Department when your review year is, and keep Digital Measures current.

exam.title: How to read the final exam schedule

sections.heading: Two schedules, two jobs
sections.text: The Registrar posts a regular schedule and a common exam schedule. The regular schedule is organized by class meeting pattern and start time. The common exam schedule is organized by course code, with one shared date, time and room for the course.

sections.heading: Regular schedule
sections.text: Find your meeting pattern (for example Monday-Wednesday or Tuesday-Thursday). Then find the row whose start-time range includes when your class begins. Read across to the exam day and the two-hour time window.

sections.heading: Common exam schedule
sections.text: Check this one first. If your course code is listed, your exam follows the date, time and room shown there, whatever your meeting pattern. Room codes use the building abbreviations in the key on the schedule (for example SBA, or TC MPH for the Testing Center Multipurpose Hall).

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Exam slots are two hours, such as 8-10 am, 11 am-1 pm, 2-4 pm and 5-7 pm. Some exams fall on weekends. Students must show their AUS ID. Make-up exams run on the last day of the exam period. Students with more than two exams in a day, more than three over two consecutive days, or a clash with a common exam should see their associate dean by the end of week 11. Every course needs a scheduled assessment in exam week.
